Vs.

full_judgment:
IV. In the previous suit filed by the appellants, the High Court Division clearly observed that the appellants have been in possession of the suit property since the lifetime of Sheikh Wahed Ali. The defendants failed to succeed up to High Court Division with their written statement case, which is similar to the plaint of Title Suit No. 70 of 2002. As Chand Ali and the heirs of Amud Ali i.e. the defendants of the suit have been admittedly in possession of major part of the suit property for a long period of at least 43-44 years, a simple suit for declaration that the impugned deed of partition is fraudulent and illegal without praying for declaration of title of the plaintiffs to the suit property and for recovery of khas possession thereof is not maintainable. The appellate court legally decided the said issue but the High Court Division without considering the aforesaid admitted facts and circumstances of the case erroneously allowed the revision and restored the unlawful judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

 a) Before rectification of the deed of partition and correction of C.S. Plot Nos. 103 and 108 to C.S. Plot Nos. 1003 and 1008, the plaintiffs had no cause of action for the suit inasmuch as, they had no apprehension of being aggrieved so as to file a suit. b) The judgment in First Appeal No. 111 of 1993 was pronounced on 10.12.2001 affirming rectification of C.S. Plot Nos. 1003 and 1008 in place of 103 and 108 in the impugned deed of partition and so, the cause of action of plaintiffs to file a suit arose firstly on that date and not prior to it. Therefore, the plaintiffs having filed the suit within three years from the date of cause of action, the suit was/is not barred by limitation under Article 91 of the Limitation Act, 1908. So, the trial court as well as the High Court Division lawfully decided that the suit is not barred by limitation. c) Although, the defendant-appellants may be in possession of part of the suit property but the same starts from the lifetime of Wahed Ali and so, the defendants failed to prove that the impugned deed of partition was acted upon. d) The defendants also failed to prove that the suit property was purchased in the name of Wahed Ali with the joint income of three brothers. Thus, the suit for simple declaration that the impugned deed of partition is forged, fraudulent, unlawful, not acted upon, etc. is the proper relief for the plaintiffs and further declaration of their title to the suit property as well as recovery of khas possession is not necessary. e) The plaintiffs' predecessor in interest Wahed Ali had purchased the suit property in the year 1924 and he was the sole owner of the same. The heirs of Wahed Ali were minors at the time of death of Wahid Ali and so Wahed Ali's step brothers had been in possession of the relevant documents of Wahed Ali. f) At the time of execution of the deed of partition, the plaintiffs were minors. The said facts are also proved by some of the witnesses. Thus, the deed of partition is apparently fraudulent and illegal. 

 11. However, Mr. Abdur Rahman finds it difficult to satisfy as to how the suit could be treated as maintainable without any consequential prayer for recovery of khas possession although the other side had/have been admittedly in possession of the major part in the suit property. 

 31. Be that as it may, on perusal of the judgment of the appellate court in Title Appeal No.11 of 2005 it appears that the appellate court considering the evidence on record correctly decided that the defendants have been in possession in the suit property since the lifetime of Wahed Ali. Therefore, the present suit for declaration that deed of partition is fraudulent, collusive etc. without any prayer for a decree for recovery of khas possession is not maintainable. Because, even if the document is declared fraudulent and illegal and the document is also cancelled, as has been done by the trial court and the High Court Division, the plaintiffs would not be entitled to get recovery of khas possession of the part of the suit property which had/have been admittedly in possession of the defendant-appellants. Therefore, the suit for declaration that the impugned partition deed is fraudulent and illegal and cancellation of the deed without any prayer for consequential relief i.e. declaration of title to the suit property and recovery of khas possession of the part of the suit property in which the plaintiffs are not in possession, is not also maintainable. But the trial court has not considered this legal issue correctly and the trial court erroneously decreed the suit. The High Court Division without reversing any material findings of the appellate court made the rule absolute, set aside the judgment and decree of dismissal of the (CIF Rtsuit g-y the appellate court and restored the erroneous judgment and decree of the trial court.
